description: Caller could not sign in after returning from leave.
work_notes: Verified identity with the fictional approved process; confirmed the account was enabled and not locked; isolated the issue to a forgotten password.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: User could not recall the current domain password. Resolution: Reset the password through the approved AD workflow and required a change at next sign-in; no password was stored in the ticket. Validation: User completed the password change and opened the Finance shared folder. User communication: Your sign-in is restored. Please use the new password only for the first login and complete the required change prompt.

short_description: Account locked after repeated sign-in attempts
description: Caller reported that Windows rejected the correct password after several attempts.
work_notes: Verified identity; queried the synthetic account state; found the account locked with no disabled flag; asked about saved credentials on the phone and VPN client.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: An outdated saved VPN credential caused repeated authentication attempts. Resolution: Removed the saved credential; unlocked the account; had the caller enter the current password once. Validation: Account remained unlocked and the caller completed Windows and VPN sign-in. User communication: The saved VPN sign-in was retrying an old password. I removed it and unlocked the account; both Windows and VPN access now work.

description: Caller received access denied for the Finance shared folder.
work_notes: Confirmed the path and single-user scope; compared approved Finance membership; found the user missing from GG-Finance after a staged account change.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Approved department group membership was omitted during a fictional account update. Resolution: Added the approved group using the lab workflow and refreshed the user's sign-in token. Validation: Caller reopened the share and created a test file in the permitted folder. User communication: Your approved Finance access has been restored and tested. No other permissions were changed.

short_description: New employee account and workstation setup
description: HR requested a Finance account and prepared laptop before the employee start date.
work_notes: Validated HR approval; manager; start time; role; location; group list; license profile; and asset stock. Tracked identity; access; cloud; MFA; and endpoint tasks separately.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Approved new-hire request required coordinated identity and endpoint fulfillment. Resolution: Created the staged fictional identity; applied approved groups; assigned NS-LT-015; and completed the documented cloud and endpoint simulation checklist. Validation: Compared attributes and access with the request; confirmed device assignment; and recorded a successful fictional first-login handoff. User communication: Your account and laptop checklist are complete for the approved start date. Contact the service desk if any first-login step differs from the guide.

description: HR requested access removal at a specified effective time and recovery of the remote laptop.
work_notes: Confirmed authoritative HR request; employee identity; effective time and time zone; manager; data-preservation need; license; groups; VPN access; and asset custody.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Approved separation required synchronized identity containment and asset recovery. Resolution: Executed the fictional timed disable; session revocation; group cleanup; preservation approval; license task; and device-recovery checklist. Validation: Identity showed disabled; access list was reconciled; manager acknowledged data handling; and NS-LT-014 status changed to Recovered. User communication: The offboarding control checklist is complete and the recovered asset is with IT. This portfolio record contains no real employee or tenant action.

description: Manager requested removal of obsolete Operations access and addition of approved Finance access.
work_notes: Verified manager and data-owner approvals; compared current and requested groups; identified one obsolete group and two approved Finance groups.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: A role change left stale access and omitted the new department baseline. Resolution: Removed only the approved obsolete group; added Finance baseline groups; retained unrelated access pending owner review. Validation: Manager and user confirmed required Finance access and absence of the former Operations share. User communication: Your approved Finance access is active and the obsolete Operations access was removed. Other access was left unchanged.

short_description: Repeated MFA prompts in Outlook and Teams
description: Caller received repeated MFA prompts in two desktop applications after a password change.
work_notes: Confirmed no unexpected sign-in alert; compared web and desktop sign-in; found stale cached application tokens limited to the client.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Desktop application tokens were stale after the fictional password change. Resolution: Signed out of affected apps; removed approved cached work credentials; restarted; and completed one new sign-in. Validation: Outlook and Teams reopened without repeated prompts during the validation window. User communication: The applications were using an old sign-in token. After a clean sign-in both apps remained connected; report any unexpected prompt or unfamiliar location.

description: Caller was stuck at the enrollment registration screen.
work_notes: Verified identity; confirmed the allowed method; checked automatic time on the phone; restarted the enrollment session; and avoided asking for a one-time code.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The phone clock was manually set and outside the accepted time window. Resolution: Enabled automatic date and time on the device and restarted the fictional enrollment flow. Validation: Caller completed the challenge and a test sign-in without sharing the code. User communication: MFA enrollment is complete. Keep approval prompts private and deny any request you did not start.

description: Caller reported a sign-in alert from an unfamiliar location and denied initiating it.
work_notes: Verified the caller through the fictional approved channel; recorded alert time; location; device text; and recent activity; instructed the caller not to approve prompts; followed the simulated session-protection step; preserved the alert; and escalated.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Tier 1 did not determine the cause; the unrecognized sign-in required Security review. Resolution: Security Operations performed the simulated investigation and closed the alert; Tier 1 maintained user communication and documented the handoff. Validation: Security recorded the simulated disposition; active sessions were reviewed; and the caller completed a clean sign-in. User communication: I protected the account within service-desk scope and sent the alert details to Security. Their simulated review is complete; contact us immediately if another unfamiliar prompt appears.

description: Caller could sign in to Windows and other services but the quality application rejected access.
work_notes: Confirmed single-application scope; reproduced the authorization message; verified network and identity sign-in; compared approved role request with the application's visible role; captured time and error text.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Application-side role mapping did not include the approved Engineering quality role. Resolution: Escalated with reproduction and approval evidence; Application Support corrected the simulated role mapping. Validation: Caller opened the application and accessed the approved test workspace. User communication: Your general account was healthy. The application team corrected its role mapping and you confirmed access to the approved workspace.

description: Caller reported that all browser pages failed while a nearby workstation worked.
work_notes: Confirmed adapter state; found an APIPA address and no default gateway; compared Wi-Fi association; renewed the DHCP lease after reconnecting to the approved network.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The client associated to a stale wireless profile and did not receive a DHCP lease. Resolution: Removed the stale lab wireless profile; reconnected; and renewed addressing. Validation: Client received the expected documentation subnet; gateway; DNS; and successful HTTPS test. User communication: The laptop reconnected to the approved network and received valid settings. Web access is working again.

description: Caller could reach the lab gateway and an internal service by IP but not by hostname.
work_notes: Confirmed valid IP and gateway; IP connectivity succeeded; hostname lookup failed; adapter showed an unapproved DNS server; captured a read-only triage sample.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The client adapter used an incorrect DNS server and could not resolve the lab zone. Resolution: Restored the approved lab DNS assignment and cleared the client resolver cache. Validation: Name resolution returned the documentation IP and the caller opened the fictional internal service by hostname. User communication: General connectivity was healthy; the DNS setting was incorrect. I restored the approved value and verified the internal name and application.

short_description: Can ping server IP but not hostname
description: Caller reached the documentation IP but the saved hostname failed.
work_notes: Validated server IP reachability; queried the hostname; found a stale negative resolver-cache entry after the lab record was corrected.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The local resolver cache retained a prior failed lookup. Resolution: Cleared the DNS client cache and retried the approved hostname. Validation: Lookup and application connection both succeeded twice. User communication: The laptop had saved an earlier failed lookup. I cleared that local cache and confirmed the hostname now works.

description: Caller lost access after moving between office floors.
work_notes: Confirmed APIPA address; no gateway; wireless adapter enabled; approved SSID visible; then disconnected and reconnected before renewing the lease.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The client did not complete DHCP after roaming between access points. Resolution: Reconnected to the approved SSID and renewed the DHCP lease; no infrastructure change was made. Validation: Expected address; gateway; DNS; and internal test connection were present. User communication: The laptop did not receive network settings after roaming. Reconnecting renewed the settings and restored access.

short_description: VPN connects but internal resource fails
description: Caller established VPN but could not reach one internal application before a customer call.
work_notes: Confirmed VPN connected; internet remained available; internal DNS resolved; TCP test to the application subnet failed; another remote user reproduced the failure; collected route and port results.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Client evidence indicated a multi-user VPN route problem outside Tier 1 authorization. Resolution: Escalated to Network Operations; the fictional resolver group restored the missing route advertisement. Validation: Two remote test users reached the internal application and the caller completed sign-in. User communication: Your VPN session was connected; the failure was on the internal route. Network Operations restored it and we confirmed application access.

description: Caller received a client connection error while home internet worked.
work_notes: Confirmed internet and time sync; checked client state and found the VPN service stopped after an update; captured the error before restart.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The local VPN client service did not restart after the fictional update. Resolution: Started the approved client service and relaunched the VPN application. Validation: VPN established; internal DNS resolved; and the approved test resource opened. User communication: The VPN background service had stopped after the update. It is running now and the internal test passed.

short_description: One approved website will not load
description: Caller could browse other sites but an approved recruiting portal showed a stale error.
work_notes: Confirmed single-site scope; resolved DNS; tested HTTPS port; opened a private window successfully; isolated the failure to cached site data.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Corrupt cached site data affected one browser profile. Resolution: Cleared only the affected site's cached data and restarted the browser. Validation: Portal loaded in the normal profile and the caller completed a test navigation. User communication: Network and DNS were healthy. I removed the stale data for that site only and confirmed the portal loads.

description: Caller had no network icon after using airplane-mode controls.
work_notes: Verified airplane mode was off; enumerated adapters; found Wi-Fi disabled; confirmed no device error before enabling it.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The local wireless adapter was disabled accidentally. Resolution: Enabled the adapter and reconnected to the approved network. Validation: Address; gateway; DNS; and HTTPS tests succeeded. User communication: The wireless adapter was disabled. I enabled it and verified network and web access.

description: Caller reported brief wireless drops several times per day.
work_notes: Collected adapter; driver; signal; power; and event details across two sessions; wired connection remained stable; updated the approved driver and disabled adapter power saving for testing.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: A dated wireless driver and aggressive local power-saving setting caused intermittent disconnects. Resolution: Installed the approved driver and applied the approved adapter power profile. Validation: No disconnect occurred during the extended validation window; event count remained clear. Resolution exceeded the simplified P3 target. User communication: I updated the approved wireless driver and power setting. The longer validation window completed without another disconnect.

short_description: Required TCP port fails from office network
description: Caller resolved the service hostname but the approved TCP connection timed out.
work_notes: Confirmed DNS; gateway; and unrelated HTTPS access; repeated the target-port test from two lab clients; captured timeouts and scope; made no firewall change.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Multi-client evidence indicated an upstream access-rule issue outside Tier 1 scope. Resolution: Escalated to Network Operations; the fictional team corrected the approved lab access rule. Validation: Port test succeeded from both clients and the application completed its connection. User communication: DNS and general network access were healthy. Network Operations corrected the approved port rule and we validated the application.

description: Caller saw a profile loading message and Outlook closed.
work_notes: Verified web mail availability; started Outlook in safe mode; isolated an approved add-in; repaired the profile after the first session did not persist.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: A damaged local Outlook profile following an add-in crash prevented normal startup. Resolution: Disabled the problematic lab add-in and created a fresh local mail profile. Validation: Outlook opened normally twice and simulated mail send/receive completed. User communication: Your mailbox was available online; the local Outlook profile was damaged. I rebuilt it and confirmed send and receive.

short_description: Outlook is not receiving new mail
description: Caller saw recent messages in web mail but not the desktop client.
work_notes: Confirmed service available and messages present in web mail; found Outlook working offline; checked send/receive and client status.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Outlook had been placed in Work Offline mode. Resolution: Returned Outlook to online mode and initiated send/receive. Validation: Three recent messages synchronized and a simulated test message arrived. User communication: The mailbox was healthy; Outlook was in offline mode. It is online now and current messages synchronized.

description: Caller could hear a meeting but no microphone appeared in Teams.
work_notes: Checked physical mute; Windows input list; privacy permission; and Teams device selection; Windows detected the headset but Teams had the laptop array selected.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Teams retained the wrong input device after the headset was reconnected. Resolution: Selected the approved headset microphone and saved the Teams device setting. Validation: Teams test call recorded and played back clear audio. User communication: The headset was available but Teams had selected another input. I selected the headset and the test call passed.

short_description: Teams sign-in fails after password change
description: Caller could sign in on the web but the desktop client repeated an authentication error.
work_notes: Confirmed account and web sign-in; checked time; signed out; cleared only the approved Teams credential cache; restarted the client.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The desktop client retained a stale authentication token. Resolution: Removed the stale local token through the approved client reset and completed a new sign-in. Validation: Teams opened; chat synchronized; and the client remained signed in. User communication: Your account was healthy. I cleared the stale desktop token and confirmed Teams is connected.

description: Caller saw a sync warning on a Finance working folder.
work_notes: Checked service status simulation; account; storage; path length; invalid characters; and client state; found one filename with a trailing period.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: A filename unsupported by the sync client blocked the folder queue. Resolution: Renamed the synthetic file according to the naming policy and resumed sync. Validation: Queue reached Up to date and the file appeared in the simulated web view. User communication: One unsupported filename blocked the queue. I renamed it to the approved format and confirmed the folder is up to date.

description: Caller received access denied for a recruiting template shared by an HR colleague.
work_notes: Verified exact link and identity; confirmed the owner intended HR-team access; found the link targeted a different fictional user; requested owner correction rather than changing repository permissions.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The sharing link was addressed to the wrong synthetic account. Resolution: The fictional owner re-shared the document with the approved HR group. Validation: Caller opened the document in the browser and desktop application. User communication: The original link was assigned to another account. The owner corrected the approved share and you confirmed access.

description: Caller saw an activation banner after switching accounts.
work_notes: Confirmed approved fictional license assignment; checked active Office identity; found a personal account selected in the application; preserved no token details.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Office was signed in with an unlicensed personal profile instead of the fictional work identity. Resolution: Signed out of the unrelated profile and signed in with the approved work identity. Validation: Activation banner cleared and two Office applications opened normally. User communication: The application was using the wrong account. I switched it to the approved work identity and confirmed activation.

short_description: Request access to shared Finance mailbox
description: Manager requested shared-mailbox access for an approved Finance responsibility.
work_notes: Verified requester; mailbox; business justification; data-owner approval; and requested permission level; made no unauthorized cloud change.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The approved request required a Microsoft 365 permission change outside Tier 1 role scope. Resolution: Escalated with approval and scope; the fictional M365 team applied least-privilege mailbox access. Validation: Mailbox appeared after the simulated propagation period and the user opened it without send-as rights. User communication: The approved access required the Microsoft 365 team. They applied read/manage access only and you confirmed the mailbox opens.

description: Caller needed video for a meeting beginning in 30 minutes.
work_notes: Confirmed physical privacy shutter; Windows camera detection; privacy permission; and Teams selection; found the shutter closed.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The laptop camera privacy shutter was closed. Resolution: Opened the shutter and selected the integrated camera in Teams. Validation: Teams preview displayed video and the caller joined the test meeting. User communication: The camera was blocked by the physical privacy shutter. Video is working and the meeting preview passed.

description: Caller reported that Word closed when opening one template.
work_notes: Confirmed other documents opened; started safe mode; disabled the template add-in; reproduced without it; captured application version and event time.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: A corrupted local template add-in caused the crash. Resolution: Removed the corrupted lab template from the startup path and restored the approved copy. Validation: Word opened the affected template twice and saved a test copy. User communication: The application was healthy; the local template add-in was damaged. I restored the approved copy and verified open and save.

short_description: Windows Update fails with storage error
description: Caller reported a repeat update failure and low-disk notification.
work_notes: Recorded update code; checked free space; reviewed update history; cleared approved temporary files; retried after restart.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Insufficient free space prevented the feature update from staging. Resolution: Removed approved temporary content and an obsolete lab installer; restarted and retried the update. Validation: Update completed; restart succeeded; and free space remained above the lab threshold. User communication: The update could not stage because the disk was full. I safely cleared temporary content and confirmed the update completed.

short_description: Computer is very slow after sign-in
description: Caller reported a 10-minute delay after each sign-in.
work_notes: Checked Task Manager startup impact; disk; memory; update state; and event timing; found two approved but unnecessary vendor utilities starting together.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: High-impact vendor startup utilities delayed the user session. Resolution: Disabled the utilities from automatic startup without uninstalling them and restarted. Validation: Interactive desktop was ready within the fictional two-minute baseline and business apps opened normally. User communication: Two optional startup utilities caused the delay. I disabled their automatic start and confirmed a normal sign-in.

description: Caller reported that a quality tool stopped launching after the latest approved update.
work_notes: Reproduced; captured application and OS versions; checked event code; tested approved repair; confirmed another updated Engineering client reproduced; documented temporary web workaround.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Client evidence showed a version compatibility issue requiring application-owner review. Resolution: Escalated with logs and reproduction; Application Support deployed a fictional compatible build. The simplified P3 resolution target was intentionally missed. Validation: Compatible build launched on two updated clients and the caller completed the test workflow. User communication: The issue affected the application build after the Windows update. The application team supplied a compatible build and testing passed.

description: Caller saw the shared printer offline while another queue worked.
work_notes: Confirmed device power through on-site contact; checked client queue; cleared one stuck synthetic job; reconnected the approved queue; monitored a second session.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: A corrupt local print job held the client queue offline. Resolution: Cleared the local job; restarted the client spooler under the approved workflow; and reconnected the queue. Validation: Test page printed and the next business document entered and left the queue normally. User communication: A stuck local print job held the queue offline. I cleared it and confirmed two successful prints.

description: Caller requested an application from the fictional approved software catalog.
work_notes: Verified catalog approval; license type; device; disk space; and absence of a conflicting version; scheduled installation with the caller.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Approved service request required standard software fulfillment. Resolution: Installed the fictional approved package through the lab workflow and recorded its version. Validation: Application opened; default file association remained unchanged; and the caller completed a sample open operation. User communication: The approved application is installed and tested. Your existing default application was left unchanged.

description: Caller received a low-storage warning before a presentation.
work_notes: Checked category usage; found approved temporary meeting recordings already synchronized; confirmed retention and user approval before local cleanup.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Redundant local copies of synchronized fictional recordings consumed the free-space reserve. Resolution: Removed only confirmed synchronized local copies and Windows temporary files; changed no retention policy. Validation: Free space exceeded the lab threshold and the presentation application opened and saved normally. User communication: I removed only synchronized local copies and temporary files. Storage is back above the support threshold and your presentation test passed.

description: Onboarding request required an approved Finance laptop and standard application profile.
work_notes: Verified approved request; user; group tag; stock; synthetic serial; duplicate status; shipping/location; application profile; and readiness checklist.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: Device deployment required Endpoint Management enrollment and compliance tasks outside Tier 1 role scope. Resolution: Escalated a complete fulfillment task; the fictional Endpoint team applied the standard profile and returned validation evidence. Validation: Asset assigned; first sign-in simulation completed; required applications present; and fictional compliance state reported healthy. User communication: Your approved laptop profile and core applications are ready. The device assignment and validation checklist are complete.

description: Caller could use the shared Operations workstation but it did not appear in the weekly inventory view.
work_notes: Verified physical asset tag; synthetic serial; hostname; location; last check-in; and source CSV; found a formatting mismatch in the source system identifier.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: A trailing space in the synthetic source identifier prevented the inventory join. Resolution: Corrected the simulated source-data formatting and regenerated the inventory view. Extended reconciliation caused the simplified P4 target miss. Validation: NS-WS-019 appeared once with the correct location and no duplicate record. User communication: The workstation was present but its source identifier did not match. I corrected the lab record and confirmed it appears once in inventory.

description: Caller reported an unexpected payroll-themed message and had not opened the link.
work_notes: Verified the report; instructed the caller not to interact; captured sender; subject; received time; and visible URL text without opening it; preserved the simulated message; searched no mailbox content beyond authorization; escalated.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The message required security analysis; Tier 1 did not determine maliciousness. Resolution: Security Operations completed the fictional analysis and disposition; Tier 1 communicated the result and documented user guidance. Validation: Security recorded the simulated disposition; no user interaction or additional reports were identified in the lab dataset. User communication: Thank you for reporting the message without opening it. Security completed the simulated review; continue to use the report process for unexpected sign-in links.

short_description: Cannot connect to meeting before executive briefing
description: Caller reported that Teams showed offline 20 minutes before a scheduled executive briefing.
work_notes: Acknowledged time sensitivity; confirmed internet worked; found Teams in offline mode after the laptop resumed; restarted only the client; provided browser-join fallback while testing.
close_notes: Root cause/finding: The desktop client did not reconnect after sleep; network and service were healthy. Resolution: Restarted the Teams client and retained the browser link as a fallback. Validation: Desktop client reconnected; test meeting joined with audio; caller entered the scheduled meeting on time. User communication: The network was healthy; the Teams client had not reconnected after sleep. It is online and the meeting test passed; the browser link remains available as backup.
